messages:
alex: FYI I pushed a new cache-efficiency dashboard to grafana — shows per-model / per-route / per-tenant prefix hit-rate, token_saved, hit_latency, eviction_rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/prefix-efficiency. Top view: trending drops for a few tenants this morning.

maria: I see a sharp eviction_rate spike for mosaic-v2-13b around 11:40 UTC and route /chat/complete hit-rate fell 0.72 -> 0.45. Not huge # of requests but big token impact. :frowning: 

kevin: interesting — we rolled runtime change 2026-03-10 that updated batching scaling and kernel selection heuristics. If batch sizing shifts average seq-length, kernel path can change and that affects how we generate cache keys (prefix length heuristics). cc @sophie

sophie: dug into traces. KV GC kicked at 11:40:21 which removed ~4200 keys and introduced a 260ms pause in cleanup loop. Log excerpt: ```kv_gc: trace=abc123 removed=4203 pause_ms=260 backlog=18``` Also tokenizer normalization change from v2->v2.1 causes slightly different prefix tokenization for some customers.

alex: thanks. can you drop the full trace id + sample request so we can correlate with replay?

sophie: trace id abc123. PromQL used for dashboard calculation: ```sum by(model,route,tenant) (rate(prefix_cache_hits_total[15m])) / sum by(model,route,tenant) (rate(prefix_cache_requests_total[15m]))``` and token-saved: ```sum by(tenant) (rate(prefix_cache_tokens_saved_total[15m]))```

maria: AcmeCorp shows ~120k tokens_saved/hour lost in the regression window (11:30-12:30). That maps to ~$0.18/hr at current billing but latency impact is visible to product.

grafana-bot: ALERT: prefix_cache_token_saved dropped 38% for tenant=AcmeCorp model=mosaic-v2-13b route=/chat/complete — alert_id=78f severity=warning

kevin: plausible root: we increased default batch scale from 512 -> 768 on canary which increases effective sequence lengths in the kernel selector. Also found key truncation logic in keygen v1 that drops suffix tokens when length > 256 — with longer sequences that results in more collisions. I repro'd with a replay of 10k requests and saw cache hit-rate drop ~27% locally.

alex: options: revert batch scaling on canary, tighten key normalization (include route+model+prefix-hash v2), or change truncation to sampled hashing rather than fixed-truncate. Which is fastest?

jamaal: suggest immediate plan: 1) revert batching default on canary (low risk) 2) enable key normalization flag (route+model+prefix_hash_v2) behind feature flag 3) schedule 24h warmup for heavy tenants after changes and compare token_saved delta. I'll coordinate with infra-ops for canary revert.

maria: also: add a tenant-slice metric 'token_saved_per_million_requests' and an alert rule: if it drops >15% over 30m, fire. That'll catch regressions earlier.

sophie: opened PR for eviction_reason labels + normalized_key v2: https://git.redwood/infer/+/2345 — it adds labels: eviction_reason, key_length_bucket, normalized_key_v2. Also tweaked GC thresholds to avoid bulk GC during traffic spikes.

alex: action items recap: @jamaal revert canary batch scale, @sophie merge PR and coordinate GC threshold tweak, @maria add tenant-slice and alert rule, @kevin run replay benchmark and share results. We'll meet in 30m at 15:30 UTC to validate dashboards. :thumbsup:

maria: one more ask — can dashboard show 95th pct token_saved impact per-tenant so we don't get skew from a few huge requests?

kevin: yes will add 95th pct slice to the query set. Also will attach replay script and seed so on-call can reproduce.

alex: great. thanks everyone. I'll pin this thread and link the grafana panel in the meeting invite.
